text:
maria: Hey — running into a strange one in the sampleapp after flipping to the new sidecar batcher helper in Node. Rerank step gets vectors with different lengths in the same response batch (two 768s + one 512), which breaks our downstream score mapping.

liam: Oof. Can you share the minimal repro + which Node SDK version and exact helper API you used? Also did you pass an explicit model for embeddings or rely on defaults?

maria: Repro: Node SDK 1.2.0, using SidecarBatcher from @devex/sdks. Code snippet (trimmed):
```
const b = new SidecarBatcher({ maxBatch: 8 });
await b.enqueue([{ id: 1, text: 'a' }, { id: 2, text: 'b' }, { id: 3, text: 'c' }]);
// batcher flush -> POST /v1/embeddings sidecar forward
```
Response shows: item0.vector.length=768, item1.vector.length=768, item2.vector.length=512. No model override in call.

sara: Two quick checks: 1) Are you sure the batch wasn't split across shards (different hosts)? 2) Any client-side retry or auth refresh happening at the same time? We've seen retries hit different model variants.

jordan: Adding context — the sidecar helper normalizer tries to be permissive: Node helper will accept both `documents` and `inputs` keys for legacy reasons, Python helper always sends `inputs`. If a retry duplicates a request and the cluster route differs, the requests could land on a quantized variant vs full model -> dim mismatch.

maria: Interesting. I captured logs: there is a brief 401 from the auth proxy, then a local token refresh and a silent retry. Log excerpt: "auth: got 401, refreshing token; retrying request (id=xyz)". That aligns with the moment the batch was sent.

devops-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T14:02:12 sidecar:v2 rolled to canary in us-west-2 :rocket:

liam: Ok triage plan: 1) capture exact outbound HTTP bodies for each enqueue/flush (curl-able reproducible sample), 2) enable X-Request-Id per-item headers so we can correlate on the server, 3) temporarily disable client-side automatic retry or make retry idempotent, 4) explicitly set `model` on the batcher config and re-run.

sara: Quick mitigation we can ship: patch the Node helper to always include `model` and `client_sdk_version` at the per-item level and add a server-side guard that rejects mixed-dimension batches with a 409 (and log route host). Will open a small PR on devex/sdks.

jordan: Filed INV-8493 (eng-runtime) to add server detection when a single batch contains mismatching vector lengths. Assigning to @eng-runtime oncall. Priority P2. Suggested fallback: split batch and score per-host then merge deterministically.

maria: Thanks — I'll pin Node SDK to 1.1.7 and disable sidecar batching in the sampleapp for now, and drop the captured HTTP bodies into the issue. Will also try Python to confirm it's Node-only. :thumbsup:

liam: Appreciate it. Once we have the request/response pairs we'll be able to see whether the retry caused dual routing or if normalizer translation introduced the mismatch. If it's a retry surface bug we may need to make retries attach a stable route header.

maria: Uploading traces and HAR in a sec. Noted on the mitigation.

sara: If anyone hits this in the wild, search for mixed-dim batches and 401+silent-retry pattern in logs — that combo is the smoking gun.

jordan: Will add an alert rule to surface mixed-dim batches to Sentry/alerts (low-volume for now).
